scenes.head: Before the plaster goes on
scenes.vo: In Nigeria, we build with block and plaster. The wires go into the wall, then the plaster goes on, and from that day, nobody can see them again. Not the owner, not the next electrician. Nobody.
Lagos Fire Service counted over one thousand six hundred fires in 2025, and electrical faults are the leading cause.

scenes.head: Fake copper: a magnet tells you
scenes.vo: Some of it is fake cable. Cable sold as copper that is really coated iron; a fridge magnet will tell you. Some of it is cable that's too thin for the breaker in front of it. And all of it gets plastered over.

scenes.tagline: A hands-free copilot for the electrician. Proof of every reading for the owner.
scenes.tag: Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon · Indie track
scenes.vo: This is WireProof. A hands-free copilot for the electrician, on the phone already in their pocket. They talk to it while they work. It reads what the camera sees, and it keeps proof of every reading for the homeowner.

scenes.head: A real board, in a real house
scenes.vo: This is a real board, in a real house.

scenes.head: Reading the board
scenes.sub: Muse Spark reads every device; code checks each rating, and asks when the print is ambiguous
scenes.vo: Muse Spark reads every breaker, left to right. Twenty-five, twenty, thirty, ten. A hundred-amp main. When the print on one breaker is ambiguous, it doesn't guess: it asks the electrician to check it by eye. And it notices what isn't there: no RCD. No earth-leakage protection on a whole house.

scenes.head: Reading a cable print
scenes.sub: The size must appear in the text the model copied, or the reading is refused
scenes.vo: Point it at a cable print and it reads the size off the sheath. But the model doesn't get the final say. Code checks that the size it reports is really in the text it copied, and that it's a size cable is actually made in. If the model isn't sure, WireProof refuses the reading and asks for a better photo. On twenty-one real photos it read twenty right, and the one it got wrong, it caught.

scenes.head: Conduit in the wall, before plaster
scenes.vo: Before the plaster goes on, it photographs the wall.

scenes.head: Mapping the wall
scenes.sub: SAM 3.1 traces each run on the block grid; Muse Image shows the wall after plaster
scenes.vo: SAM 3.1 traces every conduit run, using the blocks as a ruler. This diagonal run fails: cables must run straight so anyone drilling later knows where they are. And then it keeps the map. After plastering, the owner can still see where every cable is.

scenes.head: The agent console
scenes.sub: Every tool call, every reading, the checklist, and the electrician's sign-off
scenes.vo: Every step is on the record: what was said, what was read, what the code decided, and what is still open. The electrician signs off in the app.

scenes.head: The owner's report, on WhatsApp
scenes.sub: The verdict, the fixes in order, and the photo behind every one
scenes.vo: When the electrician signs off, the owner gets the report on WhatsApp. Not a certificate; a screening report. The verdict, the fixes in order, and behind every fix, the photo it came from. Every rule is cited. Nothing in it is the model's opinion; the model reads, and the code decides.

scenes.label: Built on Meta
scenes.head: Four Meta models do the work. Code makes every decision.

bullets.v: hears the electrician, in Nigerian English, hands-free.
reads boards and cable prints, and plans each step as the agent.
traces every conduit run in the wall, calibrated on the blocks.
shows the owner the wall after plaster, with the cables drawn in.
the privacy gate: blocks any photo with a face before it leaves the phone.

scenes.vo: Four Meta models do the work. Muse Voice Transcribe hears the electrician, in Nigerian English. Muse Spark reads boards and cables and plans each step. SAM 3.1 maps the walls. Muse Image shows the owner the wall after plaster. And Muse Spark Open runs the privacy gate, so no photo with a face in it ever leaves the phone.
